description: TCP SYN layout of the connecting host: initial TTL, DF bit, MSS, window, window scale and the order of TCP options. See README.md 'TCP SYN matching' for the notation. Signatures are tried in order and the first match wins.

signatures.label: windows-nt10
signatures.notes: Windows 10, 11 and Server 2016 and later on Ethernet (MSS 1460). Client and server versions send the same SYN.

signatures.label: windows-nt10
signatures.notes: Same layout with a window other than 64240, which is what a smaller MSS (VPN, PPPoE) or autotuning produces.

signatures.label: windows-xp
signatures.notes: Windows XP and Server 2003 send no window scale option. The window is usually 65535 or 64240.

signatures.label: linux
signatures.notes: Recent Linux kernels (and Android, ChromeOS) with MSS 1460. Window scale is usually 7 but depends on memory.

signatures.label: linux
signatures.notes: Linux 3.x and 4.x: initial window of 10 segments, advertised as 20 x MSS (29200 for MSS 1460).

signatures.label: linux
signatures.notes: Linux 2.6: 4 x MSS (5840 for MSS 1460). Still seen on old embedded devices.

signatures.label: linux
signatures.notes: Linux option order with a tuned or unusual window.

signatures.label: apple
signatures.notes: macOS and iOS (XNU). Window scale is 6 on current releases, lower on old ones. macOS and iOS cannot be told apart from the SYN.

signatures.label: freebsd
signatures.notes: FreeBSD 9 and later, and appliances built on it (pfSense, OPNsense, TrueNAS).

signatures.label: cisco-ios
signatures.notes: Connections opened by Cisco IOS itself (for example to a TACACS+ or syslog-over-TCP server).
